newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine Congress begins 1997 budget debate.
newsitem.headline: Argentine Congress begins 1997 budget debate.

text.p: The lower house of the Argentine Congress began debating the 1997 budget after noon /1500 GMT Wednesday with expectations it would pass a deficit of $3.2 billion versus $3.0 billion the government proposed.
The ruling Peronist Party was confident its majority would pass the bill with the support of provincial parties, against opposition from the Radical Party and Frepaso coalition.
But government Undersecretary of Institutional Relations, Carlos Bercun, acknowledged, "It's possible we may not end up with the $3.0 billion deficit we hoped for, we may possibly be above that."

However, lawmakers were expected to include an article in the budget bill allowing the government to slash $285 million off spending at its own discretion to allow it to reduce the 1997 budget deficit to about $3.2 billion.
Bercun said he did not know "whether it will be possible to negotiate some increase (in the deficit) with the IMF."

Treasury Secretary Pablo Guidotti has said recently that alterations to the budget bill introduced by Congress would push it $400 million over the $3.0 billion target, a shortfall which is equivalent to one percent of gross domestic product.

The Peronist government ran into a brick wall when it tried to convince provincial Congressmen to accept its proposals for 10 percent cuts in subsidies to the tobacco industry and gas supplies, which benefit them directly.
One Economy Ministry official said this failure means that "the (provincial) governors take away $1.4 billion more than last year."

The 1997 budget bill forecasts 1997 GDP growth of five percent, consumption growth of 4.3 percent and real investment growth of 10 percent. It also foresees a trade deficit of about $2.0 billion on exports of $27.5 billion and imports of $29.5 billion.
